body: ATO: You are eligible for a tax refund of $1,248. Claim within 24 hours.
redFlags: Refund offered by text from a mobile number
Link is not an official government address
explanation: The ATO does not text links to claim refunds. Check your refund inside myGov yourself.

subject: Final notice: bill overdue
body: Dear customer, your bill is overdue. Pay today or your service will be disconnected.
redFlags: Sender domain is not the real company's
explanation: Check your bill in the official app, not through an email link.

subject: Book due back Friday
body: Your loan of 'Network Security Basics' is due this Friday. You can renew it in the library catalogue.
safeSigns: Refers to a loan you actually made
explanation: A plain reminder with nothing to click. Renew through the library site yourself if needed.

body: Medicare: You are owed a $312 refund. Confirm your bank details here.
redFlags: Asks for bank details by text
Link is not an official address
explanation: Medicare does not ask for bank details by text. Use your myGov account.

subject: Grades.xlsx shared with you
body: A file was shared with you. Sign in with your university account to open it.
redFlags: Sender domain uses a zero instead of the letter o
Asks for your uni login through a link
explanation: Lookalike domains are easy to miss. Read the address letter by letter before clicking.

body: Your parcel will arrive today between 2pm and 4pm. Track it in the Australia Post app.
safeSigns: Gives a delivery window, not a demand
Sends you to the official app, not a link
explanation: Nothing is asked of you. If unsure, open the app yourself.

body: I turned $200 into $3,400 in a week. Message me and I'll show you how, small fee to start.
redFlags: Asks for a fee up front
Pushes you into a private chat
explanation: Quick-profit offers from strangers are a common investment scam.

subject: You sent $499.00
body: A payment of $499.00 was sent from your account. If this wasn't you, call 1800 000 222 immediately.
redFlags: Payment you never made, to cause panic
Asks you to call a number in the email
explanation: Call-back scams put you on the phone with a scammer. Check your account in the official app instead.

subject: Your October statement is ready
body: Your statement is ready. Log in to the YourBank app or website to view it.
safeSigns: Tells you to use the app or website yourself
explanation: It points you to the official app without a clickable shortcut.

body: Hi Mum, my phone broke so this is my new number. Can you pay a bill for me? I'll pay you back tonight.
redFlags: Unknown number claiming to be family
Avoids a call or voice message
explanation: Call your family member on their old number before sending anything.

subject: Your listing: Desk lamp, $30
body: I'll buy it now! Google sent you a code, can you read it to me so I can verify the listing?
redFlags: Asks for a verification code sent to your phone
Verification is not needed to buy an item
explanation: That code lets them take over your account. Never share verification codes.

subject: Your password was changed
body: Your password was changed today. If this was you, no action is needed. If not, go to the official website yourself and reset it.
safeSigns: Says no action is needed if it was you
Tells you to visit the official site yourself
explanation: Real security notices let you check on your own, without a link.

body: Your myki balance is negative. Top up now to avoid a $120 fine.
redFlags: Link is not the official myki site
Unexpected text from an unknown sender
explanation: Top up through the official app or machines, not a link in a text.

subject: Order confirmed: laptop $899
body: Your order for a laptop was placed. If you didn't order this, cancel within 1 hour.
redFlags: Expensive order you did not make
Link goes to a lookalike site
explanation: Check your orders by opening the official site or app yourself.

subject: Team meeting Wednesday 2pm
body: Reminder for our group project check-in, Wednesday 2pm in the usual room. Bring your progress notes.
explanation: Ordinary messages from people you know are fine. Not everything is a scam.

body: Can you vote for my cousin in this photo contest? It only takes a second!
explanation: Message your friend another way to check. Never log in through a link someone sends.

subject: New sign-in from Moscow
body: Your Apple ID was used to sign in from a new device. If this wasn't you, verify your account now.
redFlags: Scary alert to make you act fast
explanation: Check account security from your device settings, not from the email.

body: Reminder: your appointment is tomorrow at 10:30am. Reply C to confirm or call us to change.
explanation: An expected reminder with nothing to click. Call the clinic directly if unsure.

subject: You won a $1000 gift card!
body: Congratulations! Complete this 2 minute survey to claim your prize.
redFlags: Prize for a contest you never entered
explanation: Prize emails are bait to collect your details. Delete them.

subject: Work from home: $800/week
body: Receive parcels at home and repost them to our clients. No experience needed. Start today.
explanation: Parcel reshipping jobs can make you handle stolen goods. Walk away.

body: Your verification code is 482913. Don't share it with anyone.
safeSigns: You just tried to log in
Warns you not to share it
explanation: An expected login code. It's only a problem if you give it to someone else.

subject: Quick favour
body: Are you free? I need gift cards for a student prize. I'll reimburse you. Send me the codes.
redFlags: Staff member using a free email address
explanation: Real staff do not ask students to buy gift cards. Check with them in person or on official channels.

subject: Your Tuesday trip receipt
body: Thanks for riding. Your trip cost $18.40. You can see the full receipt in the app.
explanation: A simple receipt for something you did, with nothing to click.

body: Your account has been suspended. Verify your identity now to restore access.
redFlags: Login link instead of the app
explanation: Banks do not send login links by text. Open your bank app yourself.

subject: Update your details to keep payments
body: Update your details within 48 hours or your payments will stop.
redFlags: Domain is not an official one
explanation: Update details through myGov, typed in yourself.

body: Your account will be banned for copyright violation. Appeal here within 24 hours.
redFlags: Appeal form asks for your login
explanation: Real appeals happen inside the app's settings, never by DM.

subject: Your enrolment is confirmed
body: Your enrolment for next semester is confirmed. You can view your timetable by logging in to the student portal as you normally do.
safeSigns: Tells you to log in the way you normally do
explanation: Safe messages send you to your usual way in, not a new link.

subject: Concert tickets x2, $120
body: Selling two tickets I can't use. PayID payment first, then I'll email the tickets.
explanation: Use official resale sites. Paying a stranger up front is a major risk.

subject: Your order has shipped
body: Order #4821 has shipped. Track it any time from your account on our website.
explanation: A normal shipping notice for something you bought.

subject: Our bank details have changed
body: Please send this week's rent to our new account. The old one is closed.
explanation: Phone your agent on a number you already have before sending rent anywhere new.

body: Your driver Sam is arriving in a white Toyota, rego ABC123.
explanation: A normal ride update you can check against the car.

subject: Your storage is full
body: Your files will be deleted in 24 hours. Upgrade now to keep them.
explanation: Check storage from inside your account, not via email.

subject: You've won a $2,000 scholarship
body: Congratulations! Pay a $50 processing fee to release your award.
explanation: Real scholarships never charge you to receive them.

body: Hi Tom, are we still on for dinner Friday? Oh sorry, wrong number! You seem nice though, what do you do?
redFlags: Often leads to investment or romance scams
explanation: Do not reply to wrong-number texts. They are how long scams start.

subject: Your card is due to expire
body: Your Medicare card expires next month. You can order a replacement in your myGov account using the official app.
explanation: It sends you to your own account. Nothing is demanded.

subject: Your listing: Bike, $150
body: Hi! Is this still available? I can pick it up Saturday and pay cash.
explanation: A normal buyer. Meet in a public place and keep it simple.

subject: Your mailbox is full
body: Dear customer, your mailbox is full. Click to increase your space.
explanation: Email providers do not ask you to log in through email links like this.

subject: Payment received
body: We received your payment of $85 for the student services fee. No action needed.
explanation: A receipt for a payment you made.

body: Your payment failed. Update your billing details to keep watching.
redFlags: Billing update through a text link
Generic message with no account detail
explanation: Fix billing from the app or website yourself.

body: Are you coming to Alex's party Saturday? Details are in the group chat.
explanation: Ordinary friend chat. Check the group chat for details.
